Alex W: Taking over primary for tonight (2311112222). Quick summary: no sev1 active, two pages yesterday (cache pressure + model OOM), current concern is increased KV cache evictions during peak. I'm primary until 07:00 UTC. Samir is secondary. Link to my quick handoff notes: https://redwood.internal/oncall/handoffs/2311112222
Maya R: Thanks — marking on my calendar. Any customer-impacting alerts live? :eyes:
Alex W: No user-facing errors in SLO graphs, but latency tail climbing for /v1/generate. I ran quick query and saw 99p latency from 420ms -> 1.2s last hour. See logs below.
Samir P: I can take pager tonight if you need me to step into primary. Otherwise I'll stay secondary. If latency crosses 2s for >5m we should escalate.
incident-bot: [ALERT] 2311112305 - latency-surge - channel=eng-oncall - severity=warning - link: https://redwood.incidents/2311112305
Lina C: Quick checklist in runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/serve-latency
Alex W: Putting runbook pointers here: 1) Check KV cache evictions dashboard 2) Confirm autoscale headroom 3) Pin model variant fallback if quantized version cheaper
Maya R: Where's KV dashboard? I can't find it.
Alex W: https://grafana.redwood/internal/d/kv-cache/kv-evictions
Samir P: If evictions high, short remediation is to bump cache size on pool-3: `redwoodctl pool set --name pool-3 --kv-cache-mb 8192` — do this only after we confirm memory slack. See runbook step 2.
Alex W: I'm running memory snapshot now.
ops-bot: Memory snapshot started for pool-3 (job id: js-9982). ETA ~20s.
Alex W: Snapshot results: free_gb=6.8, reserved_gb=1.2 — safe to bump to 8GB KV cache. I'll apply.
Alex W:
`````
# increase kv cache
redwoodctl pool set --name pool-3 --kv-cache-mb 8192
`````
Samir P: :thumbsup: I'll watch p95/p99. If we still see tail latency, next step is routing: shift traffic away from pool-3 to pool-4 which has lower load. Command:
`````
redwoodctl router migrate --from pool-3 --to pool-4 --percent 30
`````
Maya R: Customer impact to note: one customer (acme-corp) reported slow API calls 10min ago in support ticket #5421. I've dm'ed support for correlation.
Alex W: Good — inform support if we trigger a rollback or variant fallback.
incident-bot: [INCIDENT] 2311112330 - acme-slo-degrade - severity=informational - linked_alert=2311112305
Samir P: If autoscale doesn't add pods fast enough, escalate to infra: @infra-oncall. Use runbook step 4 to request emergency burst.
Maya R: Adding infra-oncall: @infra-oncall — please standby for possible ephemeral GPU burst (pool-3)
infra-oncall: acknowledged. ETA for burst capacity 8-12 min.
Alex W: Update: KV bump applied. Monitoring p95/p99 now. Initial p99 dropped from 1.2s -> 700ms. Still above usual but trending down.
Samir P: Nice. Keep an eye on model cache hit ratio; if it drops, may need to evict LRU tuning. Runbook link: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/kv-lru-tuning
Alex W: Noted. Also documenting quick rollback: if command causes regressions revert:
`````
redwoodctl pool set --name pool-3 --kv-cache-mb 4096
`````
Maya R: Tie this into handoff: Alex, can you add any open follow-ups to the handoff doc? I'll pick them up on my morning shift.
Alex W: Done — https://redwood.internal/oncall/handoffs/2311112222#followups
Samir P: Final check: Are both primary and secondary reachable? Samir P: (I'm reachable) Alex W: (I'm on Zoom) Maya R: (available after 02:00 UTC)
Alex W: Last note: If we see model OOMs, quick mitigation is to switch to quantized variant: runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/model-oom -> `modelctl set-variant --model rwd-ggml-v1-q4_0` for canary.
Maya R: Thanks. I'll take primary at 07:00 UTC today. Samir you'll be secondary until I confirm.
Samir P: Copy that.
Alex W: Handing off. Bridge link: https://meet.redwood/bridge/2311112222
ops-bot: handoff-recorded by ops-bot for shift 2311112222 (primary=Alex W, secondary=Samir P)
Maya R: Received handoff — leaving note: check acme support ticket correlation in the morning and confirm eviction patterns.
Alex W: Signing off. Good night :wave:
